findings.claim: The append-only registry check can falsely certify immutability in a shallow clone because `git log -- benchmark/versions.lock` sees only locally available history. This conflicts with the documented another-machine workflow: fetching one recorded measuring commit does not necessarily recover the registry's complete history.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:139-153 makes all historical mappings authoritative but does not require complete history; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:283-300 documents cross-machine recovery by fetching only `measuringMetasystemSha`.
findings.fix: Have `validate-kit` detect a shallow repository and either refuse with an explicit instruction to unshallow/fetch the registry's complete history, or perform that verified fetch before checking append-only mappings. Document the prerequisite and add a shallow-clone refusal fixture.

summary: Both round-7 findings are substantively closed: HEAD must preserve every historical registry mapping, including against a simultaneous object-and-lock rewrite, and §10 now explains how another machine fetches the recorded measuring commit before using cat-file. The projection covers the shipped manifest keys in the correct halves and supports byte reconstruction under the single stated difference list; compatibility preserves all six aliases; identity, legacy resume, pinned-object comparison, ancestry, mission naming, tag integrity and mandatory CLI version pins are coherent. The remaining material gap is that the historical enforcement silently degrades in shallow clones, a normal cross-machine checkout mode, so validation needs an explicit complete-history prerequisite or refusal.
